- `tests/test_engine.py:10-11` — `assertEqual(double(2), 4)` and `assertEqual(double(-2), -4)`; both expectations are literals derived from the contract, not routed back through `double()`.

That is a real behavioral RED, not an import error.
- `engine.py`'s `source_sha256` is identical (`e77335c8…`) in the pre-repair and post-repair proofs — the repair was test-only, which is correct here.

One thing I want to be explicit about rather than bury: under the mutant, `assertEqual` raises at line 10, so line 11 never evaluates in the witness. I judged that non-blocking — the negative boundary is executed and literal-checked in the green baseline, and demanding a mutant that fails specifically at line 11 would be the per-assertion kill classifier the brief tells reviewers not to introduce. I did not treat the seeded `F-negative-boundary` receipt as an actual model review; it is a disclosed synthetic seed.
